run.command: python3 train_seq2seq.py -c new_configs/model_configs/seq2seq_model.yaml  (prerequisite step for get_results.py / vanilla_beam_search.yaml / bm pipeline)
run.output_tail: seq2seq_model.yaml specifies epoch: 150, min_epoch: 30, train_batch_size: 16 over a ~42k-example train set (e2e-dataset/trainset.csv, verified present, 42064 lines). This is a from-scratch seq2seq training run that normally needs a GPU and runs for a substantial time. The sandbox's Docker daemon has no NVIDIA Container Toolkit configured ('could not select device driver with capabilities: [[gpu]]'), so the container can only use CPU, even though the host itself reports a GPU via nvidia-smi. CPU training of 150 epochs of a seq2seq model, followed by beam-manipulator training and multiple beam-search/bleu-scoring passes (the full paper pipeline: train_seq2seq -> get_results vanilla -> get_results setup_bm_traindata -> train_beam_manipulator -> get_results bm_test -> get_results_bleu_scores) is well beyond any single 10-minute execution window and the remaining tool-call budget.
